answers.text:
*PR #217 is close.* The fix is pushed, CI is green and the CHANGELOG is updated.
• Rounding bug: fixed (integer cents)
• Tests: 6 new cases, all passing
• Waiting on: a final approval from theo-lindqvist
Once Theo approves, it can merge.

On orders of 10 or more reams, the bulk discount was computed in floating point. A discount that should be exactly *$8.055* came out as `8.054999999999999`, so it rounded *down* to $8.05 instead of up to $8.06.
The customer paid one cent more than they should have. Small, but it happens on every order where the discount lands on a half cent.

All green. The 6 new cases in `discount.test.ts` cover:
• exactly 10 reams (the discount threshold)
• 9 reams (no discount)
• discounts that land on a half cent, which round up
• 500 reams, to check nothing overflows
• a $0.00 line item
• mixed carts where only one line qualifies

It can merge as soon as theo-lindqvist approves. The order portal deploys from `main` automatically, so customers would see correct totals within a few minutes of the merge.
I won't merge it myself: the repo requires a human approval, and I think that's a good rule.

Theo left one comment: `toCents` was ambiguous about which direction it converts. I renamed it to `dollarsToCents` and added a short doc comment.
I've re-requested his review. Nothing else is outstanding.

answers.text:
Computers store most decimals approximately, the way 1/3 can't be written exactly as 0.333…. So `107.40 * 0.075` lands just under 8.055, and rounding goes the wrong way.
The fix does all the pricing math in *integer cents*: 10740 cents × 75 ÷ 1000 = 805.5 cents, which rounds half up to 806 cents, exactly. The total is converted back to dollars once, at the very end, just for display.

Why did the ream of paper get the bulk discount? Because it came in 500 strong. I'll keep working on that one.
While I'm here: the customers we overcharged now get exactly *one cent* back. Very small, very correct.
